sentences.text: Bactrosaurus was a large herbivorous dinosaur that lived in Asia between 96 and 85 million years ago, though other records place its time range from 93.9 to 72.2 million years ago.
Its femur measured 80 centimeters in length, and large vertebral spines likely supported a hump on its back.
Like other hadrosaurs, this animal could adapt to both bipedal and quadrupedal postures.
A subsequent study revealed fragments that appear to be the base of an incompletely preserved crest on Bactrosaurus.
However, recent studies suggest Bactrosaurus was likely crestless because basal hadrosauromorphs do not preserve hollow crests.
The first remains of Bactrosaurus were partial skeletons of six individuals found in the Iren Dabasu Formation of the Gobi Desert, China.
Charles W. Gilmore described and named Bactrosaurus in 1933, referencing the large club-shaped neural spines on its vertebrae.

While over 10,000 fossils were examined for tumors, the specific types found in Bactrosaurus were limited to this genus and closely related genera. Researchers suggest the tumors found in Bactrosaurus may have been caused by either environmental factors or genetic propensity.
A 2026 study of fossils collected in 2014 and 2015 suggests Bactrosaurus johnsoni exhibited herding behavior and population segregation between juveniles and adults.
Bactrosaurus is classified within the suborder Iguanodontia and the superfamily Hadrosauroidea.
